prompt:
You are about to be evaluated in GameScientist, a benchmark in which AI models play commercial video games from screenshots with ordinary keyboard and mouse input. Before the run starts we would like to interview you. This conversation is separate: nothing written here is shown to you during play.

Model under test: claude-opus-5-5.
Game: Sid Meier's Civilization VI.
About the game: Civilization VI is a turn-based empire-building game. This local run uses Standard Rules, an Ancient Era Aztec start under Montezuma, Prince difficulty and one AI opponent. Only Science Victory is enabled. The free Aztec Civilization Pack is the only enabled additional content; expansion rules and community mods are disabled. Defeat occurs if the human civilization is eliminated or another team wins. Gameplay starts from a fixed undeveloped save after one documented preparation turn.
Controls:
Use left clicks to select units, cities, menu entries and map tiles. Right clicks issue map orders for a selected unit. M selects the move command, which can then be targeted with a left click. The arrow keys pan the map. The configured input profile supplies ordinary keyboard and pointer controls, using fixed points or native Box targets as declared by that profile. Units, research and production choices use the game's visible controls. The game waits for player input between turns; no process pause is used.
Choose one ordinary physical input using the current game screenshot. Pointer targets use the native Box questions for the same screenshot. Each step dispatches the selected input once.
Group input: Choose one mouse operation, scroll or keyboard input.
  mouse_left: Left-click one visible screen target.
  mouse_right: Right-click one visible screen target.
  mouse_move: Move the pointer to one visible screen target without clicking.
  mouse_drag: Drag one visible object to a visible destination.
  scroll_up: Scroll up by one step.
  scroll_down: Scroll down by one step.
  key_return: Press the Return key.
  key_space: Press the space key.
  key_m: Press the m key.
  key_b: Press the b key.
  key_up: Press the Up key.
  key_down: Press the Down key.
  key_left: Press the Left key.
  key_right: Press the Right key.
  key_f: Press the f key.
  key_r: Press the r key.
  key_u: Press the u key.
  key_c: Press the c key.
  key_t: Press the t key.
  key_v: Press the v key.
  key_n: Press the n key.
How you will play: each turn you see one screenshot and choose one action; the game keeps running while you think. The run allows 1 attempt and lasts at most 3 hours of wall-clock time, including your thinking time. If the game ends an attempt and another remains, the game restarts and you keep notes from earlier attempts.
Scoring: 100 points, awarded only from the game's own saved progress, each milestone at most once:

answers.hardest_part: Reaching the Classical and Medieval era tech milestones (Currency, Iron Working, Construction, Engineering, Apprenticeship, Machinery, Education, Castles, Stirrups, Military Tactics) within the 3-hour wall-clock budget while operating one screenshot-action at a time through Civ VI's deeply nested UI.
answers.likely_failure: Time exhaustion before the mid-game tech tier. Each meaningful action — opening the tech tree, queuing a production item, moving a builder, responding to a barbarian — costs a full screenshot-action cycle. The 3-hour clock will likely run out somewhere in the Classical era, leaving the later 60+ points on the board. District placement (Campus, Industrial Zone, Harbor) also requires multi-step decisions I may execute incorrectly from screenshots alone.
answers.helpful_mechanics: Turn-based pacing means the game waits for me with no real-time pressure between inputs. Prince difficulty and a single AI opponent reduce the chance of early elimination or a sudden loss. Science-only victory lets me queue research single-mindedly without diverting production toward cultural or domination goals. The Aztec free Monument in each new city saves at least one production queue cycle.
answers.harmful_mechanics: Single-action-per-screenshot throughput is the dominant constraint: tasks that a human player completes in one fluid session (tech choice, production queue, two builder moves, end turn) each cost a separate cycle here, multiplying turns consumed. Builder charges are finite and easily wasted on suboptimal tile improvements if I cannot read the yields clearly from compressed screenshots. Barbarian scouts that spawn near the capital can force reactive military micro that eats budget without earning any scored milestone.
